raw_case_text:
A 47-year-old lady without significant past medical or surgical history presented to the outpatient clinic with intermittent episodes of left hypochondrial pain radiating towards the left shoulder for 2 months. She did not have associated fever, jaundice, or altered bowel habits. Some loss of appetite was noted without loss of weight. She could not recall any abdominal trauma in the recent past. Physical examination was unremarkable except for a nontender hepatosplenomegaly.
Hematological and biochemical tests were normal. Abdominal radiographs were unremarkable. Abdominal USG revealed a complex cystic lesion in the spleen measuring 4 x 8 x 6 cm with poorly defined double wall and multiple internal septations suggesting a likely hydatidosis along with enlarged fatty liver.
She was given a course of antihelminthics, vaccinated against capsulated organisms predicting possibility of a subsequent splenectomy, and asked to return a month later.
At follow-up, her symptoms persisted and repeated abdominal USG showed expanding splenic cyst measuring 9 x 8 x 8 cm. CECT scan of the abdomen showed a nonenhancing cystic lesion arising from lower pole and hilum of spleen measuring 10 x 9 x 9 cm with multiple internal septations and abutting the tail of pancreas as shown in Figure 1.
A list of differentials was considered that included a splenic hydatid cyst, pancreatic tail pseudocyst, and a mesenteric cyst. In view of clinical and radiological worsening, she was taken for an elective exploration through a left subcostal incision.
At laparotomy, a huge splenic cyst was found occupying entire lower pole and significant portion of hilum and measuring 9 x 9 x 8 cm. The aspiration of this revealed a brownish translucent fluid as shown in Figure 2, the routine bacterial culture of which was later reported to be sterile.
The cyst was causing pressure atrophy of the residual splenic parenchyma and also had multiple dense perisplenic and pericystic adhesions. Total splenectomy was done. During intraoperative manipulation, the cyst wall got inadvertently ruptured. The image of splenectomy specimen is shown in Figure 3.
She had an uneventful postoperative recovery and was discharged on the 7th postoperative day. At 2-week and one-year follow-up, she remained symptom-free.
Histopathologically, gross examination confirmed the operative findings and showed a unilocular already cut-open cyst measuring 9 x 5 cm with wall thickness measuring 2-5 mm.
Microscopic section showed a cyst wall that was composed of hyalinized fibrous tissue without epithelial lining. Also noted were plenty of extravasated red blood cells and hemosiderin laden macrophages over the cyst wall. There was no evidence of cellular atypia. The microscopic image of the SP is shown in Figure 4.
The features confirmed a SP.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 47-year-old woman presented with a 2-month history of intermittent left hypochondriac pain radiating to the left shoulder and mild anorexia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient experienced intermittent left upper quadrant pain radiating to her left shoulder and decreased appetite for 2 months without recent abdominal trauma. Despite a 1-month empirical course of oral anthelmintics, her pain persisted and repeat imaging showed cyst enlargement.
subjective.past_medical_history: Unremarkable past medical and surgical history; no recalled abdominal trauma.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for left hypochondriac pain radiating to the left shoulder and mild loss of appetite; negative for fever, jaundice, weight loss, or altered bowel habits.

objective.physical_examination: Non-tender hepatosplenomegaly; otherwise unremarkable physical examination.
objective.routine_investigations: Hematological and biochemical panels and plain abdominal radiographs were normal. Initial abdominal ultrasound showed an enlarged fatty liver and a 4 x 8 x 6 cm complex splenic cyst with an indistinct double wall and internal septations, which enlarged to 9 x 8 x 8 cm on 1-month follow-up ultrasound.
objective.advanced_workup: Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT demonstrated a 10 x 9 x 9 cm non-enhancing multiseptated cystic lesion arising from the lower pole and hilum of the spleen and abutting the pancreatic tail. Left subcostal laparotomy and total splenectomy revealed a 9 x 9 x 8 cm splenic cyst filled with sterile brownish translucent fluid; histopathology of the 9 x 5 cm unilocular cyst (2-5 mm wall thickness) showed a hyalinized fibrous wall completely devoid of an epithelial or parasitic lining, with abundant extravasated erythrocytes and hemosiderin-laden macrophages.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Primary splenic pseudocyst (false non-parasitic cyst) initially mimicking splenic hydatidosis, confirmed by sterile brownish fluid culture and histopathology showing a fibrous wall lacking an epithelial or parasitic lining. Following pre-splenectomy vaccination against encapsulated bacteria and open total splenectomy, the patient was discharged on postoperative day 7 and remained asymptomatic at 1-year follow-up.
